observations: Photo 0: close-up of a wrapped machine showing a label reading 'SHARP' and 'AR-M207' beneath the brand name.
Photo 1: side view of the same machine, still wrapped in plastic film, showing a 'digital' logo sticker and paper size labels (A4, A3) on a stack of what appear to be multiple similar units.
Photo 2: another wrapped view, same unit, no power-on, no display, no counter visible.
Machine is fully encased in plastic wrap in all three photos; no photo shows the unit powered on, a screen, or a page-count counter.
No visible photo of the drum/toner cartridges or any printed test page.

claims.evidence: No import documentation, shipping label, or history shown in any photo.
No photo of the page counter/display; machine is wrapped and not powered on.

claims.claim: New drum and toner just fitted
claims.evidence: No photo of the internal drum/toner unit or a receipt/part photo.
No test print or paper-path photo shown; machine not demonstrated running.

risks.risk: Machine may not power on or may have internal faults (common with 'as seen wrapped' resale units)
risks.proof: A video or photo of the unit powered on with display active and a test copy coming out

risks.risk: Actual page count could be far higher than claimed
risks.proof: Clear photo of the page counter/display on the control panel

risks.risk: Drum/toner may be old/worn despite claim of recent replacement
risks.proof: Photo of the drum unit and toner cartridge with visible wear/date, or purchase receipt
risks.if_unproven: priced as original/worn parts, not new

risks.risk: Hidden physical damage (cracks, missing panels, water damage) concealed by plastic wrap
risks.proof: Photos with wrap removed showing all sides and the glass platen

proof_requests: Video of the machine powered on, making a test copy, showing the page counter.
Clear photo of the drum and toner cartridge removed from the unit.
Photos with the plastic wrap removed, showing all sides, the glass platen, and the control panel.
Any receipt or import paperwork supporting 'London use' and recent part replacement.
response.reason: The Sharp AR-M207 is clearly identified by its nameplate in photo 0, but every seller claim (low usage, new drum/toner, no jams, London use) is unverifiable from the photos since the unit is wrapped and never shown running, so it must be priced at worst case as an unverified, possibly heavily-used basic B/W copier.
